approach:
Root cause: a failed check's record keeps the last 200 lines of the log whatever those lines are. For a CI log they are GitHub Actions post-job cleanup, so they push out the test runner's `failures:` / `panicked at` section. The rule sits in three places: the local run in checks.rs (line 533), `with_failure_detail` (checks.rs 361) and `detail_from_job_logs` (gh/client.rs 293). Fix once: add `checks::failure_section(text, max_lines, max_bytes) -> String`. (1) It drops the trailing cleanup block. The cut is at the first cleanup line (`Post job cleanup`, `Post Run `, `Cleaning up orphan processes`, with an optional `##[group]` prefix) found at or after an anchor. The anchor is the last runner marker (`failures:`, `panicked at`, `---- … stdout ----`, `test result: FAILED`), else the last `##[error]` line, else line 0. A cleanup-looking line printed earlier in the log therefore stays, and if the cut would leave nothing the text is used whole. (2) If the remaining lines fit, they are kept. (3) Otherwise it keeps the last max_lines lines when that window holds a marker or the text has no marker at all (today's output). (4) If the window has no marker but an earlier one exists (a cleanup form not recognised), it keeps `max_lines-20` lines from the earliest marker, a `…` line, then the final 20 lines. The final lines are kept so a trailing `error[E…]` survives, which `verify::demonstration_view` and the briefs read. These two parts cannot overlap, because the window has no marker and so the first marker lies above it. (5) Byte caps: the window path caps the end as today (`tail`). The jump path caps the head part from its start (`max_bytes*3/4`, on a char boundary) and the final lines with `tail` (`max_bytes/4`), so wide lines cannot cut off the marker. `detail_from_job_logs` calls it per readable job log with an equal share of the budget: `FAILED_TAIL_LINES / n` lines (less the `== name` header) and `FAILED_TAIL_BYTES / n` bytes. The joined text is then within the cap without a re-cut, and one shard cannot push out another. `with_failure_detail` sets aside a leading `failing units:` line (verify.rs reads it), sections the rest, and puts the line back. Redaction is unchanged and runs on the kept text. Passing checks, records and schema are untouched.

Revision answers: finding 1 is answered by the end-keeping jump path and by listing the four readers in dependents, each with a test. Finding 2 by the anchored cut, with a pinned early-cleanup-line test. Finding 3 by the head-capped jump path with a wide-lines test. Finding 4 by the per-job budget, with a two-shard test whose sections are long enough that a joined re-cut would drop shard 1.

decisions.choice: One shared `failure_section(text, max_lines, max_bytes)` in checks.rs, used by run_check (failed branch), with_failure_detail and detail_from_job_logs.
decisions.reason: All three sites store a line tail by the same rule, so one function keeps them from drifting. The budgets are parameters so the client can split them across jobs.

rejected.why: Fixes only the CI path. The local run and with_failure_detail keep the same blind tail rule.

rejected.option: Store the failures section through failed_test_names
rejected.why: It yields names only, no assertion text, and nothing for an xtask panic.

decisions.choice: Cut only the trailing cleanup block: the first cleanup line at or after the last runner marker, else after the last `##[error]` line, else anywhere.
decisions.reason: Cleanup only comes after the test step, so an earlier line printed by a test must not truncate the log. The log's real failing output is before the cleanup block.

rejected.option: Cut at the first cleanup line anywhere in the log
rejected.why: A test or earlier step that prints such a line would drop the whole failing section after it.

rejected.option: Strip lines from the end while they are cleanup
rejected.why: Post-step output such as cache-save messages is not itself recognisable as cleanup and would stop the strip early.

decisions.choice: Keep a bounded jump to the earliest marker for the case where the last-N window has no marker, and in that case also keep the final 20 lines after a `…` line. The head part is byte-capped from its start.
decisions.reason: It follows the accepted reading (the section starts at the earliest marker) and protects against a cleanup form the cutter does not recognise. The kept final lines keep a trailing `error[E` line visible to demonstration_view and the briefs. Capping the head from the start keeps the marker even with very wide lines.

rejected.option: Drop the jump and rely only on the cleanup cut
rejected.why: An unrecognised cleanup shape would hide the failing section again, since the real log forms are not in the repository to check.

rejected.option: Jump with the plain end-keeping byte cap
rejected.why: Wide lines would cut off the marker the jump was meant to keep.

rejected.option: Always start at the earliest marker
rejected.why: Drops the `== shard k/n` and `Running` context lines that existing tests rely on and changes output for logs that were fine.

decisions.choice: detail_from_job_logs sections each readable job log separately with FAILED_TAIL_LINES / n lines (minus the header line) and FAILED_TAIL_BYTES / n bytes, and does not re-cut the joined text.
decisions.reason: A joined tail lets a long later shard push an earlier shard's failing section out. An equal split bounds the total (n headers plus n times the share is at most 200 lines) and keeps every shard's section.

rejected.option: Re-cap the joined sections with tail_lines(200)
rejected.why: A shard with a near-200-line section drops every earlier shard.

rejected.option: Strip once on the joined text
rejected.why: The first cleanup block would cut off all later shards.

decisions.choice: with_failure_detail sets aside a leading `failing units:` line, sections the rest with FAILED_TAIL_LINES-1, and puts the line back.
decisions.reason: verify.rs:77 reads the first line as the header; a plain 200-line cut of prefix plus 200 lines would drop it.

rejected.option: Leave with_failure_detail as a plain call
rejected.why: It would keep dropping the prefix line for a full-length log.

steps: In checks.rs add private `is_cleanup_line(line)` (trim, strip a leading `##[group]`, then starts_with `Post job cleanup`, `Post Run ` or `Cleaning up orphan processes`) and `is_runner_marker(line)` (trimmed == `failures:`, contains `panicked at`, starts with `---- ` and ends with ` stdout ----`, or starts with `test result: FAILED`).

Add `pub fn failure_section(text: &str, max_lines: usize, max_bytes: usize) -> String` next to tail_lines, with a doc comment naming the root cause. Steps: (a) find the anchor (last marker line, else last line starting `##[error]`, else 0) and cut at the first cleanup line at or after it; if that leaves nothing, use the whole text; keep a final newline. (b) If the body has at most max_lines lines, return `tail(body, max_bytes)`. (c) Else if the last max_lines lines hold a marker, or the body has no marker, return `tail(tail_lines(body, max_lines), max_bytes)`. (d) Else (jump) take `max_lines - 20` lines from the first marker, capped from the start at `max_bytes*3/4` on a char boundary, then a `…` line, then the last 20 lines through `tail(.., max_bytes/4)`. Keep tail_lines and its test.

In run_check replace `tail(&tail_lines(&output, FAILED_TAIL_LINES), FAILED_TAIL_BYTES)` (failed branch only) with `failure_section(&output, FAILED_TAIL_LINES, FAILED_TAIL_BYTES)`. In with_failure_detail, split off a leading FAILING_UNITS_PREFIX line, call failure_section on the rest with FAILED_TAIL_LINES-1 (FAILED_TAIL_LINES when there was no prefix), and put the prefix line back. Redaction stays first.

In gh/client.rs detail_from_job_logs, for each readable job push the `== name` header when more than one is readable, then `failure_section(log, per_lines, per_bytes)` with per_lines = (FAILED_TAIL_LINES / n).saturating_sub(header).max(1) and per_bytes = FAILED_TAIL_BYTES / n. Drop the re-cut of the joined text with tail_lines and tail. Leave name and unit extraction on the full plain log as it is.

Add the checks.rs tests: cleanup after a failing section (pure function); a cleanup-looking line before the section is kept; the local-run test through run_script; no marker and no cleanup equals the old tail; marker in the window equals the old tail; jump case with an unrecognised trailing tail keeps `error[E0425]` as the last line; wide lines (40 × 3000 bytes) after a marker stay within max_bytes and start at the marker; with_failure_detail keeps the prefix first for a 300-line body; the cleanup-only text falls back to the whole text; a passing run's output is unchanged.

Add the gh/tests.rs tests: single shard xtask panic followed by 250 stamped cleanup lines (no names, panic message kept, no cleanup); two shards with sections of about 150 lines each followed by cleanup (both messages kept, at most 200 lines).
Update the ci_result.rs doc comment on FailureDetail.output_tail. Add one CHANGELOG bullet under [Unreleased] → Fixed, stating only what the diff does.

Run `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p athena-core checks`, `cargo test -p athena-core gh`, then `cargo test --locked`. Confirm the new behavior tests fail on the base by temporarily reverting the non-test source changes (git stash of the non-test files). Leave run/tests.rs unchanged.

risks.risk: A cleanup-looking line printed by a test after the last runner marker would cut the log early.
risks.mitigation: Markers are specific and matched at the start of a trimmed line (after an optional `##[group]`). The cut is only at or after the last runner marker or last `##[error]` line. A test pins an early cleanup-looking line.

risks.risk: Real Actions logs may show cleanup in forms not guessed (the repository holds no real CI log).
risks.mitigation: The jump path starts at the earliest marker when the last-N window has none, and keeps the final 20 lines. The marker lists live in one place. A test uses unrecognised trailing text.

risks.risk: The jump path drops the middle of the output (a second failing binary) between the head part and the final 20 lines.
risks.mitigation: It applies only when the window has no marker. A `…` line shows the gap. failed_tests still come from the full log. Caps are the existing 200 lines and 64 KiB.

risks.risk: Equal budget split gives each shard about 33 lines when there are 6 readable logs, and passing shards use some of the budget.
risks.mitigation: Each share still holds that shard's own failing section, which is short in cargo output. The total stays within 200 lines. Names come from the full logs.

risks.risk: Prefix handling changes a full-length reused detail from 200 lines to the prefix plus 199.
risks.mitigation: A new test pins it. Before, the prefix line was dropped for logs of 200 or more lines.

risks.risk: run/tests.rs is a listed deliverable but is not edited.
risks.mitigation: Its 200-line test is unaffected (no marker, no cleanup). The producer says so in the summary and runs it under cargo test --locked.

(a) `failure_section_drops_trailing_cleanup_and_keeps_the_failing_section`: calls `failure_section(text, FAILED_TAIL_LINES, FAILED_TAIL_BYTES)` on cargo output (`failures:`, `---- t stdout ----`, `thread 't' panicked at … assertion failed: left == right`, `test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed`, `##[error]Process completed with exit code 101.`) followed by 250 lines of `Post Run …` / `Post job cleanup.` / `Cleaning up orphan processes`. (b) `a_failed_local_run_keeps_the_failing_section_not_trailing_cleanup`: `run_script(&sh_spec(..))` with a script that echoes the failing section and then 250 `Post job cleanup.` lines and exits 1; asserts `output_tail` holds the test name and panic text and no `Post job cleanup`.
